internal_series.why: Reported separately, never merged into M-001..M-003. The external series is the contributor-experience metric; this one is the maintainer-responsiveness metric. Keeping both means a period with no outside contributors still produces a measured number instead of a row of nulls that cannot be told apart from not measuring at all.

M-101_first_human_response.note: sample of 5; too small for a trend

internal_series.not_a_rate: Deliberately a count, not a percentage. Most first-party items are a maintainer opening and merging their own work, which never waited for anyone -- expressing that as a no-response RATE produces a large number that reads as neglect and means nothing. M-002 is the rate that carries meaning, over external items.

limitations: Business hours exclude weekends but NOT public holidays.
Bots are excluded by account type and a [bot] login suffix; a human account used for automation would not be caught.
Response means a comment or review by someone other than the author. A fast formal reply does not imply resolution (guideline appendix B).
Items opened by repository collaborators are excluded as first-party. The split uses the collaborator list, so a contributor who later gains write access changes population between periods.
